correctness.rationale: For k<=4, the greatest odd squarefree abundance product is (4/3)(6/5)(8/7)(12/11)=768/385<2. For k=5, monotone prime factors and exact product bounds force 3,5,7 and q∈{11,13,17,19}; r is bounded by floor(32(q+1)/(3q-32)) = 384,64,30,25. Thus exactly 87 prime pairs are possible. Each has 16 complementary divisor pairs whose chosen/omitted sum reaches 2N iff a subset of their 16 pair weights sums to Delta=sigma(N)-2N. An independent meet-in-the-middle enumeration rebuilt all 87 candidate sets from prime enumeration and proved Delta unattainable in every case. The explicit six-prime witness 937365 has sigma=1935360 and five distinct omitted complementary pairs totaling 60630, leaving 2N=1874730. Finite certificate is exhaustive only due to the analytic reduction; source cases.csv/checker verified as actual package evidence.
residual_risks: Finite exact checks are bounded and are not substituted for the explicitly reconstructed infinite proof or analytic distribution.
